The Medicare Orthotics and Prosthetics Patient-Centered Care Act claims to fix fraud but ignores the real problem: Medicare’s systemic bloat. Banning drop shipments and streamlining coverage won’t stop the $60B annual hemorrhage from overpriced contracts, redundant administrative layers, and Big Pharma’s grip on prosthetic pricing.

This bill’s 47 endorsing organizations include groups that profit from Medicare’s broken status quo—hardly neutral arbiters. Real reform requires dismantling the bureaucracy enabling 30% overhead costs on devices, not performative oversight.

Until Congress slashes the red tape letting middlemen inflate prices, vulnerable patients remain hostages to a rigged system.

Let’s fund care, not middlemen.

AI’s potential in healthcare is real—but let’s not pretend D.C. bureaucrats are the ones driving innovation. The Health Tech Investment Act (S.1399) proves the swamp’s priorities: Section 2(a)(1) mandates Medicare pay for algorithm-based services using FDA-cleared devices, yet Section 2(b) codifies CMS’s “software as a service” policy that’s ripe for abuse.

We’re talking about Medicare Advantage plans already weaponizing AI to deny claims while taxpayers foot the bill for redundant systems. Innovation thrives when government gets out of the way—not when it layers subscription fees and invoice price mandates on providers.

Heard any hearings about slashing FDA’s 20-year-old regulatory frameworks? Exactly. Priorities.

The Rural Healthcare Transformation Fund is a start, but let’s not pretend $50B fixes systemic rot. Medicaid is collapsing under bureaucratic bloat and unchecked illegal immigration draining resources meant for citizens. Half of rural hospitals lose money—not just from underuse, but from millions added to the rolls who never paid in.

Structural reform means cutting waste, enforcing borders, and prioritizing Americans who funded the system. Throwing cash at states without accountability? That’s D.C.’s favorite bandage.

Real transformation requires slashing red tape, deporting illegals exploiting care loopholes, and redirecting every penny to veterans and taxpayers—not more temporary fixes.
